$comment: Golden cases for the MFC import (import.proto THE SERVER DECIDES). Every implementation (fc-coordinator's import and Push path, fc-mobile's store and sync engine) must agree with every case. Ids, heads and values are abstract (occ ids order by their names; o1, o2, p1, q1 are rows 1144, 1144, 900 and 555's first copies, new:k and new{row}:k later ones), times are minutes since midnight, and the rows are the import's resolved rows. `serverScenarios`: the 58-case review corpus, the design probes X-01..X-11 and the judge's probes, each as its inputs in arrival order on a server, a phone P and a tablet T: an import (`by` names the device that requests it online: it pushes first and pulls the import's transaction before it shows the review set), a spine redirect, a device edit, an answer (`resolve`, naming its `item`; `revOf` names another item's rev, a client bug), a push (`n`: only the outbox's first n entries, a batch; with each event's outcome), a pull (`n` events, a page), a restart (the device loses what it had staged and resumes from the commit cursor of the last transaction it applied) and a replay from an empty cursor; `expect` is the end state: the user facets, the figures with a pending conflict, the held edits and what each device shows. `reimports`: one import onto a seeded server (copies with their bases, figure values with theirs, and the spine's survivors); `expect` is the copies and figure values after it, the keys written, the figures carded and the unresolved rows. `review`: Ross's rules R1-R8 (2026-09-27) and the round-6 rules: each import's result (the ordered review set, the applied changes with an undo, and ImportMfcExportResponse's counters, facets_written counting the marker) and the end state (user facets, pending figure items by kind, held-edit cards (each listed edit's key, value and reason, and `more`), change entries and align-MFC entries).

reimports.name: an unchanged export writes nothing
a figure value changed only on MFC is written, with its base
a figure value changed only in the app is kept
a figure value changed alike on both sides moves only its base
a figure value changed differently on both sides is a conflict, and nothing is written
after a spine merge an unchanged export writes nothing, re-keys nothing and raises no conflict
after a spine merge a value MFC changed is written under the head its base was written under
after a spine merge a value the app deleted conflicts at the survivor, where the resolving write goes
GR-Q3: one of two owned copies marked former in the app and the Count lowered on MFC writes nothing; the other copy stays owned
MFC lowered the Count and the app changed nothing: the highest occ id is removed
MFC raised the Count: a new copy at the lowest unused ordinal
MFC raised the Count after an import removed a copy: that copy is restored, filing and all
the app added a copy and MFC raised the Count: both sides reached the same count, so nothing is written and nothing is minted (Design A: no adoption write; 2 copies either way)
the app removed a copy (the highest, by PICKS) and MFC lowered the Count: nothing is written
the Count changed differently on both sides: one card for the figure, and nothing is written, not even the copy MFC added (Design A: one decision per figure)
MFC changed the kind and the app did not: the status is written and a filing of the old kind is reset
MFC and the app both marked the copy arrived: only the base moves
MFC marked the copy arrived and the app marked it former: a conflict on its status
MFC went from two ordered to one owned and the app had marked one arrived: the arrival is kept, the other copy removed
a row gone from the export removes the copies and figure values the app did not change
only MFC removed the copies, but the app changed some of the same kind: one card for the figure, and nothing is written (Design A: one decision per figure)
Count 0 states no copies, and the row still states its figure values
a later row with the same canonical id is unresolved, and the first row stands
unresolved rows write nothing and leave their earlier copies and figure values alone
the spine now resolves the id to another figure (not a merge): unchanged heads follow, and so do the figure values
rows resolving to one survivor: MFC changed one row against that row's own base and the app did not, so the new value is written (Design A: a field base per row)
two rows' products merged after one import wrote both bases at one version: an unchanged export writes nothing, whichever head is listed first
two merged rows' bases at one version: MFC changed the row whose value is shown and the app did not, so the new value is written, with no tie (Design A: a field base per row)
after a merge the more recent base stands, as long as a row still states it: an unchanged export writes nothing

two MFC rows for one figure: the app sold row 900's copy and MFC lowered row 1144: the figure's counts agree, so nothing is written or raised (Design A: rows of one figure are compared at figure grain)
two MFC rows for one figure: the app sold row 1144's own copy and MFC lowered row 1144, the same sale: nothing is written

a removed copy with a live base beside an app copy with no base (a state Design A's own bookkeeping never produces), MFC lowered the Count: read as one sold and one bought, so nothing is written (Design A: transition matching)
the same state, MFC raised the Count: the app's changes match MFC's, so nothing is written (Design A: transition matching)

review.name: Scenario 1: one of two copies sold and settled at the last import, one wished to buy back, a disposition list configured; re-imports of the unchanged export raise nothing (app-only richness never raises by itself)

Scenario 2: MFC lowered the Count and the app did not change: applied to the untouched copy and listed with an undo; identical re-imports list nothing new; undo keeps the app side and yields an align-MFC entry that stays across re-imports

Scenario 3: the app sold one and MFC was not updated: nothing is written and one divergence entry is raised, once, across identical re-imports; "MFC is behind" yields an align-MFC entry (Count and the configured sold list) that identical re-imports never re-raise; it clears itself when MFC catches up
Scenario 3, take MFC: the tracked copy the app sold is owned again and nothing recurs
Scenario 3: a new app change re-opens an acknowledged divergence at the next import
Scenario 3: a dismissed align-MFC entry stays dismissed across identical re-imports
Scenario 4, ASK (the default): a true conflict waits in the review set, once, across identical re-imports; keep yields an align-MFC entry
Scenario 4, FAVOR_APP: the conflict is settled as keep, recorded in the summary with an undo, and yields an align-MFC entry; undo takes MFC's side and the entry clears
Scenario 4, FAVOR_MFC: the conflict is settled as take and recorded in the summary with an undo; undo keeps the app side and yields an align-MFC entry
Scenario 4, FAVOR_APP is applied only to true conflicts: an MFC-only change is still applied and listed, and an app-only change is still a divergence
Scenario 5: both sides made the same change (a sale, a score) and it settles with nothing to review, on every re-import
Scenario 5: the preorder arrived on both sides and it settles with nothing to review, on every re-import
Online-only import: the requesting phone pushes its outbox first, so the import sees its sale and writes nothing provisional

The review set right after an import is one ordered set: conflicts, divergences, then the align-MFC group, then the changes the import applied with their undo; an answered item leaves it and a skipped one stays
A held edit (X-07: the phone's late sale, after the tablet re-added a copy) is in the next import's review set; keep applies it and the next import clears the divergence it resolves

Align-MFC is derived only where the MFC id is known: a wrong-variant fix re-points o1 to H1b; H1 (MFC id 1144) diverges and, once kept, asks to take 1144 out of the collection; H1b has no MFC id and raises nothing
The requester reacts right after its import: it pulls the import's transaction first, so its sale is a knowing edit and the listed change stands (R1, R7)
The requester answers a conflict from the review set and then edits the figure: both are knowing, so both stand (R1, R7)

A spine merge ends the items of both heads; the next import raises one divergence for the merged figure, once, and keep yields one align-MFC entry that keeps the row whose copy is still owned and adds both sold rows to the list; following it by hand clears it and keeps that copy
HELD (iii) counts every answer on the figure: the tablet's late score, made before the phone undid a FAVOR_MFC settlement, is held, since its replay would change what the undo decided
An answer names its item: keep naming the held-edit card's rev as a figure item is STALE, and the same keep naming the held-edit card is accepted

A held-edit card lists whole units, oldest first, at most 16 edits: 22 held edits (a new copy and 20 tags on the copy the late sale restored) show 16, keep applies those, and the card then lists the other 6
An align-MFC entry follows the app's current side: after the phone sells another copy it asks for Count 1, not the acknowledged 2
add_to_list only for a row the entry lowers: a sale MFC already settled is not listed again when a later score is kept

An acknowledgement is kept per part: when MFC catches up on the Count only, the acknowledged score is not raised again and the align-MFC entry asks for the score alone; MFC raising the Count again is then an MFC change, applied and listed, and the score stays acknowledged
Richness on a merged figure raises nothing: a wished copy beside two owned MFC rows is what no row can express
A pending conflict ends when a later import finds the two sides agreeing: MFC takes the app's score
A pending conflict ends when a later import finds MFC back at the base; what the app is ahead on is then a divergence
undo restores a write only while it still holds the value the import wrote: the phone re-used the removed copy as a gift, so the undo is STALE and the gift stands
A change entry can be dismissed: it goes and the change stays
A row gone from the export states Count 0 on MFC's side: the app sold that row's copy and MFC dropped the row, so nothing is raised
per_copy with a field side: the listed copies keep their statuses and the disputed score takes MFC's value
The align plan moves a row to a kind no row holds: MFC's one owned row should become wished when the app sold its copy and wishes it back
Merged rows that change a field to different values are a conflict; keep yields an align-MFC action on each row
A row gone from the export whose copy the app left alone: the import removes the copy and lists it with an undo, and the response counts the row in removed
MFC marks a preorder arrived and the app did not change its status: the copy becomes owned, its filing reset to owned/default, listed with an undo, and counted as a status change
An answer is no revision: the tablet's knowing tag and new copy, made before it pulled the phone's undo, are applied (HELD (ii))
A knowing edit that makes a conflict's sides agree ends it and writes nothing: an answer naming it is then STALE, and the next import settles with nothing to review
A knowing edit that leaves MFC a change to make leaves the conflict standing and writes nothing: the phone re-owns the copy it sold, and take then makes MFC's Count true
A knowing edit that leaves MFC a change to make writes nothing: the phone drops the copy it added, the conflict stands, and the next import applies MFC's removal and lists it with its undo

HELD (iii) counts an answer only when the edit was made before its commit: the phone had applied the tablet's keep, so its later sale, late only for the next import, is replayed and withdraws that import's removal
A held-edit card's keep writes the held edit as the answer's write: the phone's held sale stands over the tablet's newer edit of the same copy
The relevance test compares live copies: a copy an import created and an undo removed is out, like one never created, so the phone's late add, made before the tablet's undo, is replayed
A by-hand reaction to a listed change: the tablet re-owns the copy the import removed, so the phone's late sale, which withdraws the change, is held (HELD (i))
A by-hand reaction to a listed change, the late sale first: the phone's sale withdraws the change, and the tablet's re-own, made before it pulled that, is held (HELD (ii))

A by-hand reaction to a conflict: the tablet sells another copy, so the phone's late sale, which turns the conflict into a divergence, is held (HELD (i)); the conflict stands, the app still ahead of MFC
A by-hand reaction to a conflict, the late sale first: the phone's sale turns the conflict into a divergence, and the tablet's sale of another copy, made before it pulled that, is held (HELD (ii))
HELD (ii) holds only a reaction to the revision: the tablet's tag on the copy the replayed sale took out, a write the revision's change leaves out, is applied, and its new copy is held
A conflict raised again after it ended has a new rev: the tablet's answer to the first, pushed after the second, is STALE
A divergence raised again after a conflict replaced it has a new rev: the tablet's keep on the first, pushed after the second, is STALE
A conflict pending across an import that finds MFC's side unchanged keeps its rev, whatever the app did meanwhile: the tablet's take, made before that import, is accepted

An MFC-only change over a figure the app is ahead on is applied and listed with its undo, and the score the app is ahead on stays one divergence; keep acknowledges it and the align-MFC entry asks for the score alone
The relevance test counts the unit's own copy: the import marked the preorder arrived, the tablet filed it, and the phone's late sale of that copy, which turns the arrival into a conflict, is held

A replay that only re-shows the app's side in an item changes no item: the phone's late sale changes how the pending divergence shows that copy, not its rev, so the tablet's knowing edit of the copy is applied
A held-edit card counts what it does not list: before any answer, the 22 held edits show as 16 listed and `more` 6

A compound reaction in one push, dismiss and sale: the tablet dismisses the listed removal and sells the copy it left, so the phone's late sale, which withdraws the removal, is held (HELD (i)), and the next identical import shows the app's side as a divergence
A compound reaction in one push, dismiss and re-add: the tablet dismisses the listed removal and adds a copy by hand, so the phone's late sale, which withdraws the removal, is held (HELD (i))

A compound reaction in two pushes, dismiss and re-own: the tablet dismisses the listed removal, the phone's late sale arrives and withdraws it, and the tablet's re-own of the removed copy, made before it pulled that, is held (HELD (ii))

A compound reaction in two pushes, undo and sale: the tablet undoes the listed removal, the phone's late sale arrives and withdraws the removal, and the tablet's sale by hand, made before it pulled that, is held (HELD (ii)); the copies end as if the phone had pushed first

A compound reaction on three devices: the tablet undoes the listed removal and a third device, shown the same change, sells a copy by hand; the phone's late sale, arriving between, withdraws the change, and the third device's sale is held (HELD (ii))

A revision is what the replayed late edits alone change: the phone pushes a late tag with its undo of the listed removal, and the tablet's knowing tag on the removed copy, made before it pulled that push, is applied
Reaction clause (b) alone: the tablet, shown a copy the import added and no item, adds one of its own, so the phone's late add, which the import would have matched instead, is held (HELD (i))
A divergence whose values change between imports takes a new rev: the tablet's keep on the old one, pushed after, is STALE and the divergence stays
A change entry raised again, identical, after it ended has a new rev: the tablet's undo of the first removal, pushed after the second, is STALE
A push whose late edits are all held is no revision: the phone's late sale is held behind the tablet's re-own, and the tablet's new copy, made before that push, is applied
An undo moves no base: MFC added a copy, the tablet undid it, and when MFC adds another the app's undo stands against it as a conflict

A device that saw an item only after it ended did not react to it: the phone's sale, made after the divergence it was shown had ended, is no reaction, so the tablet's late cancel of the same copy is replayed and the divergence it brings back is shown

Reaction clause (c), an item the two placements end differently: the phone re-owns one of the two copies the import removed and listed; the tablet's late cancel of that copy and sale of the other, in one push, change the listed removal either way, and both are held (HELD (i))
HELD (ii) applies a figure value made before a revision: the tablet's knowing score, made before it pulled the phone's late sale, is no reaction and is applied

A compound reaction to an item an earlier import raised, in one push: the tablet takes the divergence the phone's late sale ends at import 3 and sells its added copy by hand, so the phone's sale is held (HELD (i), the item judged from import 3 on)

A compound reaction to an item an earlier import raised, in two pushes: the tablet takes the kept divergence, the phone's late sale arrives and ends it, and the tablet's sale of its added copy, made before it pulled that, is held (HELD (ii), the item judged from the revision's import on)

A compound reaction to an item an earlier import raised, on two devices: the tablet takes the kept divergence and a third device, shown it, sells the added copy by hand; the phone's late sale arrives between and ends it, and the third device's sale is held (HELD (ii))

HELD (ii) judges an edit late for a later import: the tablet re-owns the copy import 2 removed and listed, import 3 runs before it pushes, and the phone's late sale, arriving first, withdraws the removal, so the re-own is held

HELD (ii) judges an added copy late for a later import: the tablet adds a copy by hand while a divergence is pending, import 3 runs before it pushes, and the phone's late sale, arriving first, revises the figure, so the added copy is held
A revision that changes nothing holds no added copy: the phone's late tag goes with its held sale, and the tablet's new copy, made before that push, is applied

A device that saw no item did not react to one raised after its edit: the tablet's sale, made while nothing was pending, meets the conflict a later import raises, and the phone's late sale, which gives that conflict a new rev, is replayed
A favor_app change entry raised again, identical, after it ended has a new rev: the phone's undo of the first settlement, pushed after the second, is STALE

An item a replay withdrew and a later replay gives back at the same rev is pending with that rev again: the third device's dismiss of the align-MFC entry, which the phone's late sale withdrew and the tablet's late re-add gave back, is accepted

Two late units of one push never excuse each other: the phone's late sale and added copy each withdraw the copy import 2 created and listed; the tablet, shown that change entry, sold the created copy by hand, so both units are held (HELD (i), the push's later units at their arrival)

Two late units of one push never excuse each other, a knowing filing: the tablet files the copy import 2 created on a shelf; the phone's late sale and added copy each withdraw that copy, so both are held (HELD (i), a write to a copy the two placements leave different)

Two late sales of one push never excuse each other: import 2 removed o2 and listed it, the tablet re-owned o2 by hand, and the phone's late sales of both copies, either alone, withdraw that removal, so both are held (HELD (i))

Reaction clause (c), an item the two placements end differently, though both pass through the rev the device saw: a third device sells by hand while shown the align-MFC entry, and the phone's late added copy, which ends that entry at another rev, is held (HELD (i))

Reaction clause (c), an item the other side has pending only after a knowing edit: the tablet sold by hand while shown the align-MFC entry, and the phone's late added copy, which gives that entry the same rev once the tablet's sale is in, is applied

Keep on a conflict follows its rev, in one push: the tablet sells the copy it added, so the app's counts are back at base, and keeps; the disputed counts stay at the app's side, nothing is removed, and the align-MFC entry asks for Count 2

Keep on a conflict follows its rev, in two pushes: the tablet sells the copy it added and pushes, then keeps; the disputed counts stay at the app's side, nothing is removed, and the align-MFC entry asks for Count 2
Keep on a conflict, the control: the tablet keeps with no edit since the import; the app's three copies stand and the align-MFC entry asks for Count 3
MFC lowered the count, ASK: the app added a copy, MFC removed one, and take removes the highest copy MFC tracks; the same export then raises nothing

MFC lowered the count, FAVOR_APP: the settlement keeps the app's side; its undo is the take the import would have written, against the bases before the settlement's realignment, so it removes the same copy as take, and records the acknowledgement as take does, so the same export raises nothing
MFC raised the count, ASK: the app sold a copy, MFC added one, and take brings back the sold copy MFC tracks, then makes one new copy
MFC raised the count, FAVOR_APP: the undo of the settlement brings back the sold copy, as take does, and makes one new copy, not two
The undo of a favor_app settlement works against the export of the import that made it: a later import moved the bases and kept the entry, and the undo still takes the settling import's side
A held-edit card's keep writes knowing edits: keeping the phone's held copy makes the conflict's sides agree, so the conflict ends
A held-edit card's rev is the edits it lists: a late copy held after the tablet pulled the card joins it, so the tablet's keep of the card it saw is STALE

A tag is one unit with the push's other edits of its key: the tablet's tag, put on before a revision withdrew the tagged copy, holds its removal of that tag, made after it, in the same push (HELD (ii))

A revision leaves out only the facets its late edits write: the phone's late move of a copy to another figure also undoes the import's conversion of that copy, so a tag on it made before the revision is held (HELD (ii))

Keep follows its rev across an identical import: the tablet sells the copy it added, an import of the same export keeps the rev though it finds the counts MFC's change alone, and keep leaves the disputed counts at the app's side
Keep follows its rev across an identical import, on two devices: the phone keeps the card it pulled before that import, and the card's keep preview still writes nothing
A conflict's keep preview follows its rev: after the tablet sells the copy it added, the card still previews keep as writing nothing, and keep writes nothing
Keep leaves a disputed field at the app's side though a knowing edit brought it back to its base
Keep leaves the counts as the app has them when the app has changed them since the rev found them MFC's change alone
Keep leaves a field the rev found MFC's change alone as the app has it when the app has changed it since
Keep applies a field the rev found MFC's change alone when the app has not changed it since
Keep leaves a field the rev found alike as the app has it, though a knowing edit since put it back to its base
Keep leaves the counts the rev found alike as the app has them, though a knowing edit since put them back to their base
What keep applies of MFC's change is the import's: a copy it restores is no longer one an import removed, so after the user cancels it MFC's next added copy is a new one
take removes a copy with an origin before one without, then the highest occ id: a tracked hand copy whose id sorts above stays
The undo of a favor_app settlement puts back only the bases its realignment moved, so a copy MFC came to track since keeps its base: the undo brings back the sold copy and makes no other
The undo of a favor_app settlement puts back only the bases its realignment moved, so a hand copy MFC came to track since stays tracked: the take removes the copies with an origin first
A favor_app change entry lists as its undo the take its import would have written
The undo of a favor_app settlement realigns the bases, so MFC's later changes are decided against export 2's side
The undo of a favor_app settlement is take, not a divergence's take: a note written by hand since, which MFC never changed, stays
per_copy takes its field side for a field the rev lists as disputed, though a knowing edit since brought it back to its base
The undo of a favor_app settlement puts back a row's absence: a row new to the settling export has no base again, so the take writes MFC's score from it
What keep removes of MFC's change is the import's: the copy it takes out is one an import removed, so MFC's next added copy restores it
